newsitem.title: UK: Med Aframaxes steady/firm on lack of June tonnage.
newsitem.headline: Med Aframaxes steady/firm on lack of June tonnage.

text.p: Mediterranean 80,000 tonne dirty tanker rates were steady to firm on Tuesday on a shortage of tonnage for the rest of June, brokers said.
"There have been no new requests...but June positions are at a premium. In July there are more vessels," an Italian broker said.

He said two Croatian vessels had been fixed for Repsol at W125 on Monday evening and that the market was now climbing to the W130/135 area. "But I don't think it will go much higher than this," he added.

The inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne (Aframax) sector was quiet, but some brokers said it too showed a firm tone, with scope for rates to rise to around W130 from W120 currently, depending on loading area and dates.

Very large crude carriers, meanwhile, were steady at W72.5 on Japan or South Korea voyages, but some 2.5 points softer to Singapore and Europe at W65 and W57.5 respectively. "There simply isn't enough business," one broker said, referring to the drop in rates.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCC rates were flat at W67.5, while 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) on this route and in the Med were also little changed at W87.5/90.
Fuel oil eased, with 25,000 tonnes inter-UKC at W225 and cross-Med at W190 on a lack of enquiry, brokers said.
The Caribs/upcoast market was quiet, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes edging down to W170 from W175 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems flat at W192.5, brokers said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
